Invite path: short-phone shows client-side validation ('Enter a phone number with country code (e.g. +1…)') and a valid +14155550111 whatsapp call returns open_url wa.me correctly (verified via pytest + UI). /team from You→you-team navigates to /team showing Sam T 'Joined · 6/24/2026' + Tracker QA 'Invited · 1h ago' + Sent + Resend + team-invite-btn — full parity with web. Backend pytest: 12/13 PASS on the new test_iteration128_mobile_chats.py (the one FAIL is my own /api/me health check hitting a nonexistent endpoint — login itself succeeds; all business-relevant endpoints pass: /api/me/workspaces, /api/workspace/switch, /api/folders, /api/workspace/members, /api/workspace/model-presets, POST /api/chats direct+group, POST /api/chats/dev, POST /api/invites/phone whatsapp+sms, POST /api/contacts/match hashes-path AND raw_contacts fallback). One functional-but-latent mobile bug found in NewChatSheet.findFriends(): sends {raw_contacts:[…]} without the required `hashes` field — will 422 on real device once contacts permission is granted; helper hashPhone() is defined but never called. Not reproducible on web-preview (Contacts.getContactsAsync fails first) but must be fixed before native release.

minor.issue: Backend correctly supports both `hashes` (client-side sha256) and `raw_contacts` fallback for the workspace owner. When hashes=[] and raw_contacts is provided, the server hashes locally and returns 200 — no issue. Just a note: /api/me is 404 (health check should use /api/auth/me or /api/users/me).

ui_bugs.issue: POST body sends {raw_contacts: raw.slice(0,1000)} with no `hashes` field. Backend Pydantic model has `hashes: List[str]` as a REQUIRED field — call will 422 on a real device once native Contacts permission is granted. The file already imports expo-crypto and defines hashPhone() at lines 36-38 but never calls it. Reference: /app/mobile/src/components/NewChatSheet.tsx:168. Fix: build `hashes = await Promise.all(raw.map(async r => hashPhone(normalizePhone(r.phone))))` and send `{hashes, raw_contacts: raw}` (raw_contacts kept for the owner-side server-hash convenience).

action_items: MOBILE HIGH: In /app/mobile/src/components/NewChatSheet.tsx:168, replace the payload with `{hashes: await Promise.all(raw.map(r => hashPhone(normalizePhone(r.phone)))), raw_contacts: raw.slice(0,1000)}` so the required `hashes` field is populated. This is the reason expo-crypto and hashPhone/normalizePhone helpers were added — they must actually be called.

OPTIONAL: Add a wa.me/sms flash confirmation to the NewChatSheet after the deep-link opens — currently on web-preview Linking.openURL() fails silently (no whatsapp/sms app registered) and the user gets no feedback beyond the sheet closing itself. On mobile-native this is fine, so LOW priority.
critical_code_review_comments: NewChatSheet.tsx imports and defines contact-hashing helpers but never invokes them — dead code that also silently breaks the feature on native. This is exactly the kind of drift a small unit-test on the outgoing payload would catch.

chat/[id].tsx is still ~1733 lines. Iter127 flagged this and the pickerHint fix landed as a single useState — good enough for now but a PickerModal/PresetsBar extraction would prevent the next recurrence of the same class of miss.

Chat filter chips + workspace selector are conditionally rendered on `workspaces.length > 1` — good; but the folder-chip row uses `folders.length > 0` while apiGet('/api/folders') may fail silently and set [] — consider surfacing a soft warning if load errored so users don't wonder where their folders went.

rca of the issue: The pickerHint useState was added at chat/[id].tsx:85 as recommended in iter127. Verified via grep (setPickerHint used at 1245, pickerHint read at 1270, declaration at 85). Mobile app restart already picked it up (mobile supervisor uptime = 2m36s at test time). Contacts payload bug RCA: NewChatSheet.tsx imports expo-crypto and defines hashPhone() but findFriends() at line 168 calls apiPost with `{raw_contacts: raw.slice(0,1000)}` only — the hashes array is never computed. Backend contract requires the `hashes: List[str]` field (Pydantic-required) — server accepts empty hashes only when raw_contacts is also present AND the caller is the workspace owner, but the mobile client never sends the hashes key at all so validation fails at the Pydantic layer before the fallback runs.
